detail: Set before BEGIN, sqlite3 runs the pragma in autocommit and it is cleared before the first DELETE — sluice's first fix attempt failed exactly that way (cell PR #11, b4d8530). Later generalised to the whole load in PR #14 because fixtures load alphabetically (grants.json before organisations.json). The negative test must distinguish deferred from disabled: mutating to PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF kept the suite green until a dangling-org_id-fails-at-COMMIT test was added (PR #14, 9ae4fd0).
text: python -m services.seed --reset died with a raw FOREIGN KEY IntegrityError once users.org_id referenced a fixture-owned table — DELETE-then-reload needs PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys ON set INSIDE the explicit BEGIN, not before it.

detail: seed_demo_users() continue'd past existing rows, so only fresh DBs got org_id. Fix (PR #11): backfill when the column is NULL ('never assigned'), never overwrite non-NULL (a decision), never rewrite password_hash/role. General rule: when a migration adds a column the seeder owns, the seeder must define upgrade semantics, not just insert semantics.

detail: toggle_complete and toggle_assignment_complete write completed_at via datetime.now().isoformat() (machine-local, naive), while created_at defaults to SQLite's datetime('now') (UTC, naive). clock.to_local_date / today_service.local_date_of assume every naive timestamp is UTC (brain/time.md's documented rule) -- correct for created_at, wrong for completed_at whenever location_tzid is actually configured, since it double-converts an already-local value near a day boundary. No observable bug while location_tzid is unset (both are read as naive wall-clock with no conversion). Out of scope for zimmy-life-tracker-lqg.9 (those two routes are explicitly 'do not change'); worth its own bead to make completed_at UTC like every other _at column.
text: completed_at (toggle_complete/toggle_assignment_complete) is naive machine-local time, not UTC like created_at -- brain/time.md's naive-is-UTC rule misreads it once location_tzid is set.

detail: Seen on this Windows machine: requesting --window-size=390,1800 against a file:// page measured window.innerWidth=500 inside the page; requesting 900 measured 884. The final PNG is exactly WxH pixels (confirmed with PIL), but is a left-crop of a layout done at the wider internal width, not a resize -- so a row whose action button is right-aligned via margin-left:auto lands past the crop boundary and is invisible in the screenshot even with zero real overflow. Confirmed by injecting a debug div reading document.body.scrollWidth vs document.documentElement.clientWidth: they were equal every time (390 vs 390, then 500 vs 500, then 884 vs 884), meaning no overflow at whatever the true internal width was. Trust that equality check, not the screenshot pixels, when verifying phone width with this tool on this machine; or use --headless=new, or drive a real dev server over http:// instead of a static file:// page.
text: Chrome's legacy --headless=old --window-size=W,H --screenshot writes a WxH PNG but lays the DOM out at a different, wider internal width and left-crops it -- do not read the crop as an overflow bug.

detail: clock.to_local_date (and its db-free copy services/today_service.py::local_date_of) does 'if tz is None: return parsed.date()'. created_at is naive UTC (SQLite datetime('now')), so with no location_tzid it is measured as a wall clock against clock.today(), which is the MACHINE's local date -- a task added after 20:00 in America/New_York is filed under tomorrow and vanishes from added_today. Confirmed live: with location_tzid='' a task whose created_at was 2026-09-26 03:30 UTC (= 23:30 local) was absent and one at 2026-09-25 02:00 UTC (= yesterday 22:00 local) was present. The tz-aware config is correct for created_at and wrong for completed_at, because the complete routes write datetime.now().isoformat() (naive MACHINE-LOCAL, see f-20260925-d368d0) -- one helper cannot serve both columns, so the writer has to be fixed first.
